import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# $a(n) = (\text{smallest prime} > n^2) - n^2$

The difference between the smallest prime strictly greater than $n^2$ and $n^2$.

*References:*
- [A053000](https://oeis.org/A053000)-/

namespace OeisA53000

/-- $a(n) = (\text{smallest prime} > n^2) - n^2$. -/
noncomputable def a (n : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  (sInf {p | Nat.Prime p ∧ n ^ 2 < p}) - n ^ 2

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_0 : a 0 = 2 := tsub_eq_of_eq_add <| IsLeast.csInf_eq <| by decide

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_1 : a 1 = 1 := tsub_eq_of_eq_add <| IsLeast.csInf_eq <| by decide

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_2 : a 2 = 1 := tsub_eq_of_eq_add <| IsLeast.csInf_eq <| by decide

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_3 : a 3 = 2 := tsub_eq_of_eq_add <| IsLeast.csInf_eq <| by decide

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_4 : a 4 = 1 := tsub_eq_of_eq_add <| IsLeast.csInf_eq <| by decide

/--
Conjecture: $a(n) \le 1 + \phi(n)$ for $n > 0$. This improves on Oppermann's conjecture, which says
$a(n) < n$.
- Thomas Ordowski, Dec 17 2014
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem conjecture (n : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n) : a n ≤ 1 + n.totient := by
  sorry

end OeisA53000

findings.description: The docstring attributes the conjecture to “Thomas Ordowski, Dec 17 2014” (line 51), but the cited OEIS entry credits this comment to Jianglin Luo, September 22, 2023. This is a citation mismatch only; the Lean inequality and its domain match the source.
findings.source_evidence: OEIS A053000 states: “Conjecture: a(n) <= 1+phi(n) = 1+A000010(n), for n>0. This improves on Oppermann's conjecture, which says a(n) < n. - Jianglin Luo, Sep 22 2023.” Read at https://raw.githubusercontent.com/oeis/oeisdata/main/seq/A053/A053000.seq; the November 2023 snapshot has the same attribution.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the attribution line with “- Jianglin Luo, Sep 22 2023”. No mathematical statement needs changing.

sources_consulted: Mathlib at the supplied checkout: Mathlib/Order/Lattice/Nat.lean; Mathlib/Data/Nat/Find.lean; Mathlib/Data/Nat/Totient.lean; Mathlib/Data/Nat/Prime/Defs.lean; Mathlib/Data/Nat/Prime/Infinite.lean.
review.notes: All seven declarations were checked; no mathematical misformalization was found. The OEIS web page returned a browser challenge, so its official data mirror was used. Lean checks in /workspace/review/scratch.lean prove that the prime set is always nonempty, its infimum is the intended least prime, and subtraction never truncates. A provably equivalent computable definition matches the first 40 OEIS values and satisfies the bound for 1 ≤ n < 500. Boundary checks confirm that n = 1 is valid and n = 0 must be excluded. All five existing test proofs are sorry-free. The source still labels the bound a conjecture, consistent with the recorded open status.
